maya: Hey — noticed a sudden p99 latency jump on prod runtime around 12:07 UTC. Not the usual noisy-tenant disk IO pattern, looks correlated with one tenant's traffic pattern.
ben: Which queue/lane? any logs or traces yet?
maya: p99 from ~4.2s -> ~9.8s, throughput down ~30%. Affected model: gpt-like-14b-quant. Queue: short-seq lane but the workload has a lot of tool-call streaming. Runtime logs show repeated KV evictions + rewarm loops.
liam: grabbed a profiling snapshot. Kernel selector started choosing the slower "attention-v2" kernel for some requests where seq_len < 200. That shouldn't happen — average seq len in that tenant is ~80.
esther: kernel-selector v3 was rolled last week — could be a mis-tuned threshold for streaming cases (tool-calls append tokens after initial estimate).
maya: runtime trace example:

```
[trace] req=abc123 seq_len=78 tool_calls=3 streaming=true kernel_selected=attention-v2 kv_hits=18 kv_evictions=7
```
ben: that's suspicious — kernel mismatch + KV thrash. Batcher appears to be overpacking streaming requests with longer-tailed ones; streaming sessions inflate seq_estimate because of tool callbacks, so we end up selecting long-seq kernel.
liam: perf-bot profile shows higher GPU memcpy and slower execution time for attention-v2 at these short seqs. Looks like the selector has a bias that hurts short sequences when tool_calls present. Suggest we revert selector v3 to v2 as immediate mitigation.
perf-bot: :warning: Automatic alert: kernel-selector rollout metric shows 0.76 mismatch rate for short sequences. Recommended action: rollback kernel-selector v3 for stable lanes.
esther: short-term plan:
1) toggle kernel-selector to safe-mode (prefer attention-v1/v2 fallback)  
2) reduce max_batch_size for this tenant's queue to avoid overpacking streaming tool sessions  
3) enable KV prefix pinning for active tool-call chains (soft-pin)
maya: I'm toggling selector to safe-mode now.
maya: rolled selector back to v2. p99 started decreasing within ~60s — from ~9.8s -> ~3.5s and trending to ~2.1s.
ben: great. For medium-term fix we should: fix seq estimation for streaming/tool calls, add per-tenant batching caps, and add a kernel-selection reason field to traces.
liam: also propose KV-cache heuristic change: don't evict prefixes that are part of an active tool-call session (soft-pin for ~30s). That should cut rewarm churn.
esther: can we add quick metrics: percent_of_requests_with_tool_calls, avg_seq_estimate_error, and kernel_mismatch_rate? Add them to the runtime dashboard so on-call can spot this pattern.
maya: agree. I'll file a follow-up to capture kernel selection reason in traces (why it chose a kernel and which heuristic fired).
ben: I'll own the batching heuristic change — aim for an experiment tomorrow EOD (reduce packing of streaming sessions, add per-tenant max_batch_size override).
liam: I'll prototype KV soft-pin PR and run a micro-benchmark.
esther: I'll add the dashboard panels and wire alerts. Filing tickets now.
esther: Tickets: #1234 batching-heuristic-streaming, #1235 kv-soft-pin, #1236 trace-kernel-reason. Linking in the incident channel.
maya: thanks everyone — monitoring looks stable for the last 10m. Will escalate if we see another spike. :thumbsup:
ben: nice catch, good rollback. We'll follow up with postmortem and perf numbers.
liam: adding a small note: when we patch selector, add unit tests for streaming token-growth scenario (tool-calls that append tokens after start).
